correctness.rationale: For all finite connected positive-weight undirected graphs with pinned leaders, the stationary covariance has trace P=tr(L_ground^{-1}Σ)/2. Differentiation yields d_iP=-(GΣG)_ii/2<=0 for PSD Σ and d_ijP=G_ij(GΣG)_ij. A grounded Laplacian has nonnegative inverse; entrywise-nonnegative Σ gives every mixed derivative nonnegative and hence finite-set supermodularity. For any Σ_ij<0 a graph with large s grounding and one i-j follower edge has d_ijP=cΣ_ij s^-4+O(s^-5)<0, uniformly over a pair of unit candidate-edge additions. Direct 2x2 inversion gives the sharp rho_* criterion and the exact negative gap -1/200 for a positive-definite Σ. The packaged standard-library checker passed 8686 exact-rational assertions; it corroborates but does not establish infinite quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The closest same-object paper Xu--Zhang 2023 uses independent white noise and derives supermodularity for an unweighted inverse trace. The present result characterizes exactly which correlated, fixed covariance matrices preserve that guarantee over every positive-weight grounded network, and proves loss for every negative cross-covariance. Earlier independent-noise leader-selection and ungrounded-coherence papers do not cover this iff statement. Standard inverse-positivity and differentiation are not independently novel; related unindexed theorems remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: Generality of inverse-positive matrix derivatives means a differently phrased existing result may imply the nonnegative-covariance sufficiency statement.
The available literature search and published research-record search are bounded, so uniqueness/publication priority is not certified.
The characterization is universal over graphs; negative noise correlations do not force failure for each individual fixed graph.

value.rationale: Supermodularity provides the diminishing-returns structure behind greedy edge-selection guarantees in published noisy DeGroot leader-follower design. Shared disturbances can have negative cross-correlations, raising a motivated robustness question. The iff identifies the exact covariance sign class that preserves this guarantee on all networks, separates it from unconditional variance monotonicity, and yields an explicit positive-definite two-follower counterexample plus sharp tunable correlation boundary. This is a model-level structural boundary, not an arbitrary parameter slice, elementary normalization check or standalone known-table recomputation.
